subject: general
question:
**Change the following from active to passive: **

Have the engineers resolved the calibration issue yet?

options.text: Has the calibration issue had been resolved by the engineers yet?
Has the calibration issue been resolved by the engineers yet?
Has the calibration issue be resolved by the engineers yet?
Has the calibration issue resolved by the engineers yet?

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Have the engineers resolved the calibration issue yet?"
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the calibration issue" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "have resolved" to "has been resolved" (present perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the engineers."
 
• Ensure the word "yet" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"Has the calibration issue been resolved by the engineers yet?"*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Has the calibration issue had been resolved by the engineers yet?" – Incorrect use of "had" (incorrect tense).
 
• **Option 3: **"Has the calibration issue be resolved by the engineers yet?" – Incorrect verb form "be" (missing "been").
 
• **Option 4: **"Has the calibration issue resolved by the engineers yet?" – Missing auxiliary verb "been."
